objective.stem: Exercise means the physical activities that
objective.answer: make the body move and work
distractors: keep the body on the chair
make us sleep in the day

objective.stem: A game is an organised activity with
objective.answer: rules, played for fun

objective.stem: Exercise makes the heart and the
objective.answer: lungs work well

objective.stem: A child who plays and exercises
objective.answer: sleeps better at night

objective.stem: Games teach discipline because I
objective.answer: wait for my turn and listen for the whistle
distractors: shout at my partner and push in front
leave the ground before the game ends
keep my eyes shut while I run

objective.stem: Egg and spoon race trains the
objective.answer: hand and the sense of balance
distractors: ear and the power of hearing
nose and the smell of things
back and the power of bending

objective.stem: In the egg and spoon game, if the ball falls we
objective.answer: pick it up and continue

objective.stem: In a sack race the player
objective.answer: stands inside a sack and jumps to the line
distractors: runs beside a sack full of sand
carries the sack on the head for a friend
hides inside a big sack at the line

objective.stem: In the three-legged race, the pair must
objective.answer: walk as one, with the inside legs tied
distractors: jump over each other's legs twice
carry one another to the finishing line

objective.stem: Musical chairs and freeze dance are both games of
objective.answer: movement and stopping on a signal

objective.stem: Stretching the body means
objective.answer: reaching for the sky and touching the toes
distractors: holding the breath for a long time

objective.stem: Skipping is done with a
objective.answer: rope, jumping forwards and then backwards
distractors: ball, thrown up to a partner
sack, jumped inside to the line
stick, carried slowly across the ground

objective.stem: Leaping is a big jump
objective.answer: from one foot to the other foot
distractors: from both feet onto one mat

objective.stem: The safe way to land from a jump is with
objective.answer: soft, bent knees

objective.stem: Body conditioning means exercises that make the body
objective.answer: fit and in good control

objective.stem: Arms are stretched sideways while balancing because they
objective.answer: act like the beam of a scale

objective.stem: While balancing on one leg, a good trick is to
objective.answer: count slowly to ten

objective.stem: Walking heel to toe on a line drawn on the floor trains the
objective.answer: balance of the body

objective.stem: Kicking, hitting, bouncing and rolling are
objective.answer: manipulative movements

objective.stem: An underhand throw is made with the arm
objective.answer: swinging from behind and low

objective.stem: The safest object to throw and catch in class is a
objective.answer: bean bag

objective.stem: Catching is done with
objective.answer: two hands out, eyes on the object all the way to them
distractors: one hand only, with the eyes on the ground
the head and the two shoulders together
the knees and the feet of the player

objective.stem: The brain and its wires working with the muscles is called
objective.answer: neuro-muscular

objective.stem: A dance routine is
objective.answer: the same order of steps done again and again
distractors: a single jump done only once in the day
a slow song with no movement at all
a game played with a ball and a bat

objective.stem: A forward roll is started from a
objective.answer: squat, with the two hands placed on the mat
distractors: standing jump, with the legs kicked high
lying down, with the back flat on the floor
full run, with the arms swinging fast

objective.stem: A roll must be done on a mat or soft ground because
objective.answer: a hard floor can hurt the neck and the back
distractors: the mat is colourful and clean to look at
the floor of the class is dusty
soft ground is faster for running

objective.stem: Sport develops flexibility, which is the ability to
objective.answer: bend and stretch easily

objective.stem: Agility is the ability to
objective.answer: move quickly and change direction
distractors: hold a pose for a long time

objective.stem: Reaction is shown when
objective.answer: the ear hears the clap and the leg starts to run
distractors: the eye closes slowly at the time for sleep
the hand holds a pencil on the exercise book
the mouth tastes the food we eat at home

objective.stem: Strength is built by
objective.answer: exercise and play

subobjective.stem: Mention four things exercise and games do for the body.
State four basic games we played in class.
Name four body exercises in the stretching lesson.
Give three rules for fair play in a game.
points: no taking another's place; say "well played" to a loser

subobjective.stem: Mention three ways of walking we learnt.
points: on tiptoe or on the heels

subobjective.stem: State four safety rules for throwing and catching.
Name the two parts that work together in a neuro-muscular skill.
Give three things needed for a good balance.
Mention four qualities sport develops in a child.
State three rules we keep in the rolling area.

theory.stem: Write on the importance of exercise and games to a child of my age
Describe three games we do in class and what each one trains
Explain the difference between leaping and hopping, and say how to land safely
Write on throwing: name the two throws and give two safety rules
Describe how a forward roll is done and state two rules for doing it safely
